title: Count the digits with a do-while loop

blocks.text: How many times a loop runs is not always known in advance: dividing a number by 10 until nothing is left takes as many passes as the number has digits.
Write `count(long n)` in `Digits`. It returns how many decimal digits `n` has, ignoring its sign:

items: `0` is written with one digit, so `count(0)` is `1`;
the sign is not a digit: `count(-120)` is `3`, and `count(Long.MIN_VALUE)` is `19`.

blocks.text: A `do`-`while` loop fits: its body runs once before the condition is checked.

cases.says: count(0) is 1: the body runs once before the check.

concepts: A do-while loop checks its condition after the body, so the body always runs at least once.
While loops fit work whose number of iterations is not known in advance.
